text:
ACI APAC & MID Encourages Greater Airport Readiness to Scale Sustainable Aviation Fuel

(Airports Council International) Scaling Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) to multi-location operations requires more than production, it demands robust supply chain and infrastructure readiness across airports in Asia-Pacific and Middle East.

At the recent SAF APAC Summit 2026 in Melbourne, Australia, Airports Council International Asia-Pacific & Middle East (ACI APAC & MID) joined industry stakeholders to address the role of the airports in enabling credible carbon accounting, accelerating Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) infrastructure readiness, and stakeholder alignment.

Speaking at the panel: "Sharing a Cleaner Sky: Building a Regional SAF Network," Ken Lau, Head, Sustainability, ACI APAC & MID, shared insights on regional SAF corridors. As APAC nations are progressing at varying paces in SAF deployment, a regional network creates vital synergy, to leverage each other’s strengths in implementing SAF. Though traditionally the concept of regional SAF corridor involve large hub airports, but we should not neglect other regional airports that could have location advantage for SAF deployment.

Ken also emphasised the importance of harmonising policy across diverse jurisdictions, which could be supported by establishing national and regional SAF coalitions and stakeholder task forces that helps align industry positions and streamline engagement with governments.

The discussion also centres on the best practices of major hub airports in developing SAF, while the geographical advantage of smaller regional airports in deploying SAF should not be overlooked, the distinct location advantages includes the proximity to feedstock sources or direct port infrastructure, making the airports ideal nodes for regional SAF distribution.

ACI APAC & MID remains committed to facilitate this transition by advocating for harmonised policy frameworks and empowering its airport members to bridge national readiness gaps, through a pragmatic and collaborative approach to building a more resilient and sustainable aviation ecosystem. title: Hawaii Renewable Fuels Ramp-Up to Drive PARR's Long-Term Growth
description:
Par Pacific is expanding beyond conventional refining through Hawaii Renewables, which could become an important long-term growth driver.
The facility is designed to produce 61 million gallons of renewable diesel, sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and renewable naphtha annually using PARR's existing infrastructure.
PARR completed its first commercial renewable diesel sales, creating a pathway for future revenue growth.
Valero Energy Corporation VLO and Chevron CVX have exposure to renewable fuels through different approaches, with VLO emphasizing large-scale renewable diesel production and CVX pursuing a broader lower-carbon fuels strategy.

text:
Par Pacific Holdings, Inc. PARR is a leading refiner with 219,000 barrels per day in refining capacity and a diversified portfolio spanning refining, logistics, retail and a 46% interest in Laramie Energy. Par Pacific is expanding beyond conventional refining through Hawaii Renewables, which could become an important long-term growth driver. The facility is designed to produce 61 million gallons of renewable diesel, sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and renewable naphtha annually using PARR's existing infrastructure.

Hawaii Renewables produced on-specification renewable diesel in April 2026, marking an important operational milestone. Its flexibility to produce up to 60% SAF or 90% renewable diesel allows Par Pacific to adjust its product mix based on market demand. Production ramped during the second quarter, with June throughput reaching approximately 3,000 barrels per day before the plant-wide turnaround. PARR completed its first commercial renewable diesel sales, creating a pathway for future revenue growth.

The joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation and ENEOS Corporation further strengthens the project's prospects, with the partners contributing $100 million for a 36.5% interest. The joint venture provides feedstock-sourcing and customer-access capabilities across Asia-Pacific and California. Par Pacific has not yet provided mid-cycle earnings guidance for Renewables as it continues the commissioning and ramp-up process. As utilization and commercial sales increase during the ramp-up, Hawaii Renewables could emerge as a meaningful growth engine and diversify PARR's earnings over the longer term.

Are VLO & CVX Producing Renewable Fuels?

Valero Energy Corporation VLO and Chevron CVX have exposure to renewable fuels through different approaches, with VLO emphasizing large-scale renewable diesel production and CVX pursuing a broader lower-carbon fuels strategy.

Valero's renewable fuels portfolio is anchored by its Diamond Green Diesel (DGD) joint venture, which has 1.2 billion gallons of annual renewable diesel capacity. In its latest earnings call, VLO reported a sharp improvement in its renewable diesel business, with operating income of $717 million, against a $79 million loss a year earlier, while sales volumes averaged 3.8 million gallons per day.

Chevron is strengthening its renewable-fuels portfolio as part of its broader lower-carbon strategy. CVX's renewable-fuels portfolio is well-positioned to benefit from its existing infrastructure and conventional fuel technologies.

text:
Aug. 17, 2026

A Colorado-based company that at one point had announced a $2.6 billion ethanol-based jet fuel plant in South Dakota has pulled away from the state.

In its most recent earnings report, Gevo confirmed it is exiting the project in South Dakota, known as ATJ-60. It held a ceremonial groundbreaking in the fall of 2022.

The proposed facility was one of several biorefineries that would have been connected to a proposed carbon capture and sequestration pipeline from Summit Carbon Solutions, which ended up facing legal and regulatory challenges.

Gevo instead is investing its capital into North Dakota facilities.

“Our carbon business strategy is working, and Gevo North Dakota is a strategic asset for profitable growth,” CEO Paul Bloom said in a statement.

“Exiting our ATJ-60 project in South Dakota and other non-core projects and recognizing a one-time, non-cash impairment reflects our disciplined approach to prioritize the most attractive near-term growth while enabling long-term value creation.”

Gevo had planned to build on 245 acres near Lake Preston.

The recent quarterly earnings report included a one-time non-cash impairment charge of $176 million related to capitalized development costs and reflecting the decision to exit all activities related to low-carbon ethanol and sustainable aviation fuel production in Lake Preston to focus on capital projects at Gevo North Dakota, just outside Richardton in the western part of the state.

“Our Gevo North Dakota complex is better suited to support a strategic platform growth than the Lake Preston, South Dakota, site we were previously developing,” Bloom said on an earnings call.

“Gevo North Dakota combines one of the strongest active on-site carbon capture and sequestration capabilities in the world, with access to advantaged local feedstocks, established rail and truck logistics, an experienced operating workforce, available land and pore space capacity for future growth, and it’s in a business-friendly state that supports agriculture, energy and carbon management.”

The move resulted in a second quarter net loss of $77 million, or 75 cents per share, though gross profit for the first half of the year ending June 30 was $36 million, compared with $21 million in the same period last year.

“Gevo delivered strong second quarter operational results and unlocked significant carbon business revenue that is expected to begin in the third quarter,” Bloom added.

The company improved its full year 2026 outlook to anticipate earnings exceeding $60 million, more than double the previous target.

“Gevo has a powerful growth platform centered on commodities, carbon and incentives,” Bloom said. “We have focused development around our existing operations, improving margins and near-term cash flow, with a portfolio of growth projects that we believe will create substantial shareholder value.”

text:
(Alliance News) - Hydrogen Utopia International PLC on Monday said it obtained a licence which strengthens its partnership with InEnTec Inc.

The London-based company, which transforms non-recyclable waste plastic into hydrogen, clean fuels and advanced materials, said it secured a licence from InEnTec to deploy its proven plasma-enhanced melter gasification technology for sustainable aviation fuel production across the UK.

The licence agreement, with a total consideration of USD500,000, grants Hydrogen Utopia the right to build, operate, and scale PEM Melter systems throughout the UK, among other things.

Of the total sum, USD250,000 has been paid, and the remaining USD250,000 is payable by promissory note.

Hydrogen Utopia said the licence agreement is secured as the UK government increases support for domestic low-carbon fuel production.

Hydrogen Utopia Chief Executive Officer Aleksandra Binkowska said: "We are delighted to strengthen our partnership with Inentec, which operates the only commercially proven technology in its class. This positions us well for expansion into the UK, where the government is actively supporting the sustainable aviation fuel market. We expect to now accelerate our UK operation as we engage with feedstock suppliers, off take agreements and finalise discussions on location for the SAF facility."

Hydrogen Utopia shares rose 5.9% to 2.17 pence each on Monday afternoon in London.

title: Targeting SAF at a handful of major airports could deliver outsized climate and health ...
description:
The report, Maximizing the Climate Co-Benefits of Sustainable Aviation Fuel via Targeted Allocation, analyzed 2024 flight activity at major U.S. and European airports to identify where targeted SAF use would have the biggest impact.
The report models the effect of blending SAF at these six airports at rates from 10% to 100%.
At a 50% blend, contrail-related warming fell by 30% to 34% at the U.S. airports studied and 33% to 40% at the European airports, while particulate emissions during landing and takeoff dropped 26% to 28% at all six locations.
“The health benefits alone make a strong case for targeting,” said Lucía M. Maroto, transportation decarbonization manager for Europe at CATF and a co-author of the report.
“Our analysis shows that targeted SAF use could reduce particulate pollution around major airports, helping to limit exposure in the communities most directly affected by aviation’s air-quality impacts.
text:
A new report from Clean Air Task Force finds that directing sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) to a small number of high-impact airports, rather than spreading it across the aviation network, could significantly increase the fuel’s climate and public health benefits while global supply continues to build. The report, Maximizing the Climate Co-Benefits of Sustainable Aviation Fuel via Targeted Allocation, analyzed 2024 flight activity at major U.S. and European airports to identify where targeted SAF use would have the biggest impact.

“Every ton of SAF reduces carbon emissions no matter where it’s used, but that’s not true of the fuel’s other climate and health benefits,” said Thomas Walker, associate director for transportation technology at Clean Air Task Force and a co-author of the report. “Contrail formation and local air pollution are both highly dependent on where and when a plane takes off. That means a relatively small amount of SAF, directed to the right airports, could do far more good than the same amount spread evenly across the system – especially while SAF supplies are highly limited.”

Working with aviation climate data company Estuaire, CATF analyzed 16.6 million flights at major U.S. and European airports in 2024, examining contrail formation as well as particulate matter and nitrogen oxide emissions during landing and takeoff. The analysis found that just 2% of flights generate 80% of contrail-related warming, meaning a targeted approach can capture most of the climate benefit without requiring a large share of the global SAF supply, which made up just 0.7% of the jet fuel market in 2025.

Based on a combination of contrail impacts and air quality benefits, the report identifies John F. Kennedy International Airport, Los Angeles International Airport, and O’Hare International Airport as priority U.S. locations for targeted SAF allocation. In Europe, London Heathrow, Istanbul Airport, and Paris Charles de Gaulle were identified for the same reasons. JFK and Heathrow stand out as both operating large numbers of long-haul, internationally distributed flights that regularly cross ice-supersaturated regions over the North Atlantic, where contrails form most readily.

The report models the effect of blending SAF at these six airports at rates from 10% to 100%. At a 50% blend, contrail-related warming fell by 30% to 34% at the U.S. airports studied and 33% to 40% at the European airports, while particulate emissions during landing and takeoff dropped 26% to 28% at all six locations.

“The health benefits alone make a strong case for targeting,” said Lucía M. Maroto, transportation decarbonization manager for Europe at CATF and a co-author of the report. “Our analysis shows that targeted SAF use could reduce particulate pollution around major airports, helping to limit exposure in the communities most directly affected by aviation’s air-quality impacts. Given that baseline air-pollution mortality in Europe runs two to three times higher than in the U.S., the public health case for targeting major hubs such as Paris Charles de Gaulle and Heathrow is particularly strong.”

text:
Brussels, August 17, 2026 – Brussels Airlines launches scheduled passenger flights to Evenes (Norway), Kemi and Kittilä (both Finland). These destinations are added to the winter timetable, as holidays to the arctic in winter are becoming increasingly popular. In addition to scheduled passenger flights, Brussels Airlines also operates charter flights to the arctic region in cooperation with travel agencies.

Kittilä will be offered three times weekly between December 10 and March 27. Kemi is offered up to twice weekly in the schedule between December 25 and March 10, Evenes is executed once weekly in February and March.

“The arctic region in winter is no-less than magical. Brussels Airlines has been offering these winter wonderland destinations in cooperation with travel agencies, but as demand grows, flights to the region will from now on also be offered as scheduled passenger flights, allowing travellers even more choice to discover outdoor adventures and distinctive local culture.”

​ -Greet Vandebos, Head of Leisure Sales, Brussels Airlines

Nordland and Lapland offer untouched natural landscapes and is ideal for observing northern lights during the winter months. ​

Tackling seasonality

Demand in the aviation industry is highly seasonal, with the summer months as peak season. Brussels Airlines has been working on tackling this seasonality with a variety of measures, such as student cabin crew members to increase productivity during the peak season, but also by adding attractive winter destinations.

Since winter 2024, Brussels Airlines offers four destinations in the Canary Islands during winter, with the addition of Fuerteventura. Also, Funchal in Madeira was added to the schedule as a destination with year-round mild temperatures.

As of this year, the Nordics are the newest addition to the winter timetable in order to offer an attractive leisure network, year-round.

Tickets are on sale on brusselsairlines.com and via travel agencies.

title: Russia begins deliveries of import-substituted Il-114-300 turboprops - Aerospace Global News
description:
Russia announced first Il-114-300 turboprop deliveries According to an announcement by Russia’s First Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov, the first russified Ilyushin Il-114-300 deliveries have begun.
The official Russian news outlet, Obyasnyaem RF, quoted Manturov as stating, “We are beginning the first deliveries of the Il-114-300 aircraft.
The regional turboprop typically comes with a 66-seat baseline capacity.
The Il-114-300 has strict initial operating conditions The Ilyushin Il-114-300’s type certificate, issued by the Federal Air Transport Agency (Rosaviatsiya), includes strict limitations that may significantly affect its operation.
Cold weather and relatively austere airfield operations are almost the raison d’être of the Russian regional aircraft requirement.
text:
Russia has said it is delivering the first import-substituted regional Ilyushin Il-114-300 turboprops, which are a rough analogue to the Dash 8/Q400 and ATR-72-600. Deliveries in 2026 and 2027 are expected to be minimal and come with very tight operating limitations.

Russia announced first Il-114-300 turboprop deliveries

According to an announcement by Russia’s First Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov, the first russified Ilyushin Il-114-300 deliveries have begun. In June, Russia reissued the type certificate for the Il-114, with Manturov saying at the time that Rostec has modernized almost all of the aircraft’s systems.

The official Russian news outlet, Obyasnyaem RF, quoted Manturov as stating, “We are beginning the first deliveries of the Il-114-300 aircraft. Serial production of the updated Tu-214 is ramping up, and the MC-21 and Superjet are in the final stages of testing and certification.”

He is reported to have added, “The creation of a modern civil aviation fleet is of key importance here. Today, this program is moving into practical implementation.”

In November 2025, AGN reported that the first russified legacy Soviet Tupolev Tu-214 airliner was being prepped for delivery, although that particular aircraft was in business configuration.

While the delivery numbers were not announced, they appear to be very modest.

In June 2026, Russia’s Kommersant reported, “Transport Minister Andrei Nikitin announced that delivery of three Il-114-300s is expected in 2026 and approximately the same number in 2027, with production capacity to increase thereafter.”

Russia’s import-substituted regional turboprop

The Il-114 is the post-sanctions variant of the Soviet-origin aircraft. Its development started in 1982, and first flew in 1990. The regional turboprop typically comes with a 66-seat baseline capacity. It replaces ageing Antonov An-24 and An-26s.

Interestingly, Kommersant adds, “It boasts lower fuel consumption than its foreign competitors, ATR and Bombardier.” Some Russian sources claim it has 16% lower fuel consumption than the ATR 72-600, but there is no good public data to back up these claims or to establish exactly what is being compared.

Kommersant added that Russia’s Aurora, an airline based in the Far East, is not expected to get its first aircraft until 2028. Aurora is expected to be one of the biggest customers for the aircraft with an order for 20 examples.

The Il-114-300 is produced with Russian Klimov TV7-117ST-01 turboprop engines and avionics, while the older Il-114-100 was produced with Canadian Pratt & Whitney engines and foreign-made avionics. Around 20 of them were built at the Tashkent Aircraft Plant in Uzbekistan.

The Il-114-300 has strict initial operating conditions

The Ilyushin Il-114-300’s type certificate, issued by the Federal Air Transport Agency (Rosaviatsiya), includes strict limitations that may significantly affect its operation. It is intended to operate in Russia’s austere Arctic and Siberian regions and replace the An-26 and An-24s already operating there.

According to the type certificate data sheet, it is only certified for operation in a rather narrow band of favourable weather conditions. This includes a temperature range of -9 to +25°C (the older Il-114-100 was certified for -30 to +45°C).

While Russian/Soviet aircraft are famously built for rugged conditions, the turboprop 114-300 is also prohibited from operating in icy conditions and thunderstorms. The initial certificate permits takeoff and landing only from runways with artificial surfaces.

Airport elevations are limited to -300 meters to +1,000 meters; the latitude is set to ±70°, while its crosswind certification is just 15 m/s (dry), 12 m/s (wet).

These limitations, which effectively say “don’t operate it in cold, icing, or stormy conditions or on unpaved runways,” have drawn online mockery. Cold weather and relatively austere airfield operations are almost the raison d’être of the Russian regional aircraft requirement.

The limitations are its initial certification, and these are expected to loosen over time.

description:

Warp News has followed Heart Aerospace since the company's early years and has written about it several times.

text:
Heart Aerospace's demonstration aircraft X1 flew for the first time, staying in the air for 27 minutes.

The electricity for the flight cost about five dollars.

The production version, the ES-30, is expected to cut operating costs by more than 40 percent compared with today's regional aircraft. The aircraft is in the same size class as a commercial regional airliner.

27 minutes in the air over the Champlain Valley

Early in the morning at Plattsburgh International Airport in upstate New York, an aircraft rolled out onto runway 35. What happened next had never happened before: a battery-powered aircraft in the same size class as a commercial regional airliner took off and flew.

The flight took place on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, and lasted 27 minutes. The aircraft, named X1, was flown by one pilot and reached 1,100 feet above the ground, roughly 335 meters. The powertrain, running entirely on batteries, delivered more than one megawatt of power. The test profile included taxiing, takeoff, climb, maneuvering and landing.

The flight was conducted under a special airworthiness certificate in the experimental category, issued by the US aviation authority, the FAA. The certificate came in July 2026 and gave permission to begin flight testing immediately. The test flights take place within a defined envelope: no more than 140 knots, no more than 2,000 feet above the ground and no more than 1.5 G in maneuvering load.

Plattsburgh is a regional commercial airport serving a community of 20,000 residents. That is exactly the kind of traffic Heart Aerospace is aiming for.

Warp News has followed Heart Aerospace since the company's early years and has written about it several times. The first time was in September 2020, when founders Anders Forslund and Klara Andreasson showed off their electric motor in a hangar at Säve airport outside Gothenburg and had a handful of employees. Warp News has since visited the hangar together with readers and reported on the company's steps from drawing board to flying machine.

Five dollars of electricity against a jet fuel price up 63 percent

The X1 used about $5 worth of electricity on its first flight. The figure says something about why Heart Aerospace is building electric aircraft at all.

Over the same period, the price of jet fuel rose sharply. In the week ending August 7, the average price was $3.50 per gallon, or about $0.92 per liter. That is an increase of 63 percent compared with a year earlier. Electric propulsion decouples airlines' operating costs from the swings in the global oil markets.

"With the first flight of X1, Heart Aerospace has demonstrated electric flight at the size of a commercial airliner," says Anders Forslund, founder and CEO. He describes the company's goal as abundant flight: more, cheaper and cleaner flights to and from airports closer to where people live.

What the X1 was meant to prove

The X1 is not intended to be sold. It is a full-scale demonstrator representing the production aircraft, the ES-30, and it was built to verify technology, aerodynamics, flight performance and the company's own ability to carry out an aircraft program.

Heart lists the steps the program has gone through. The company has designed an airframe from the ground up around electric propulsion, verified the new geometry through simulation and physical testing, developed its own components, and integrated electric motors, batteries, power electronics, control systems and avionics into a flying aircraft. The airframe has been load-tested to its limits and the powertrain has been tested under flight-like conditions.

Added to this is a flight test organization with staff, procedures and analytical capability, along with an established working relationship with the FAA on airworthiness.

"Through the X1 program, Heart has built the capability to design, build, test, operate and continuously improve an all-new electric airliner," says chief technology officer Ben Stabler. That capability is now being carried over to the ES-30.

The size of the aircraft

The X1 measures 32.3 meters between the wingtips, 23.2 meters from nose to tail and 7.3 meters in height. Its takeoff weight exceeds 11,340 kilograms. That makes the X1 the largest battery-electric aircraft ever to have flown.

Propulsion comes from four electric motors mounted on the wings. The aircraft has a T-tail. At the aircraft's unveiling, a cabin mock-up for 30 passengers and a cockpit mock-up were installed on board.

ES-30: 30 seats, 200 kilometers on electricity and 800 kilometers on hybrid power

The ES-30 is a conventional fixed-wing aircraft with 30 seats and hybrid-electric propulsion. It is being developed for certification under the FAA's Part 25 rules, which apply to larger airliners.

According to the planned specifications, the ES-30 will fly 200 kilometers fully on battery and 800 kilometers on hybrid power, with 25 kilograms of baggage per passenger and a 30-minute charging time. The hybrid system is based on two turbogenerators that, according to Heart, will run on sustainable aviation fuel. They provide an energy reserve and supplement battery power on longer legs. These are design targets, not flight-verified performance.

Heart expects the ES-30 to deliver more than 40 percent lower operating costs per aircraft than older regional airliners. The company points to four reasons: lower energy costs, less maintenance thanks to simpler electric propulsion and electrified systems, higher availability through an integrated electronics and software architecture, and low exposure to the emissions-related taxes and fees that are growing in aviation markets around the world.

The range is suited to short routes. In North and South America there are 5,000 airports and a network dominated by routes under 500 miles, or about 800 kilometers. In Europe, the same range covers large parts of the continent.

From a 1:5 scale model to full-scale flight

The road here has come in clear steps. Heart Aerospace started in 2018 with two people in hangars at Säve airport outside Gothenburg.

The first aircraft was called the ES-19 and was a planned 19-seat all-electric regional airliner with a stated range of up to 400 kilometers. On December 17, 2021, the company flew an unmanned 1:5 scale model of the ES-19 at Säve. The model had a 4.6-meter wingspan, flew for four and a half minutes and reached a top speed of 150 kilometers per hour. In parallel, a full-scale powertrain demonstrator had been ground-tested for more than a year.

In September 2022, Heart set the ES-19 aside and instead presented the 30-seat ES-30 with hybrid propulsion. This was a new product configuration rather than a scaling up of a finished aircraft. Earlier orders from United and Mesa were, according to the company, confirmed for the new model.

From early on, the strategy was about avoiding unnecessary risk. The company chose not to design an entirely new aircraft in every respect, but to use proven parts and adapt what is required when batteries and electric motors replace jet fuel and piston engines. "The principles of aircraft design are low speed, low altitude, conventional design to be safe, low risk, boring and easier to certify," said Philip Keenan, then head of airworthiness and certification, during a visit to the hangar in 2022.

The airlines that have put money in

The ES-30 has customer commitments from United Airlines, Air Canada and JSX. Heart says the combined customer commitments amount to $9.4 billion.

"The first flight of X1 is a major technical achievement for Heart Aerospace, a company United has been proud to support," says Michael Leskinen, chief financial officer at United Airlines. He points out that electric airliners can deliver a better travel experience for passengers while also strengthening the airline's business.

John Di Bert, deputy group chief executive and chief financial officer at Air Canada, describes the X1's first flight as an important milestone. "Our investment in Heart Aerospace and the ES-30 reflects Air Canada's commitment to supporting innovative technology that has the potential to change aviation," he says.

The next step is being built in Los Angeles

Heart Aerospace is headquartered in Los Angeles. There, the company is now developing the first pre-production example of the ES-30 in its pilot factory.

Flight testing of the ES-30 is planned to begin in 2028. Type certification and entry into service are set for 2031.

text:
Hydrogen Utopia International PLC (LSE:HUI) has obtained a UK licence from U.S.-based InEnTec Inc. to use its PEM gasification technology in the production of sustainable aviation fuel, expanding the company's footprint in the waste-to-fuel sector.

The licence, valued at $500,000, allows Hydrogen Utopia to develop and operate systems across the United Kingdom that transform non-recyclable plastics, waste tyres and other discarded materials into syngas suitable for producing sustainable aviation fuel (SAF). The agreement builds on an existing exclusive licence covering the Middle East and North Africa.

The expansion into the UK comes as government policy increasingly supports the development and adoption of lower-carbon aviation fuels. The UK Government is implementing its Low Carbon Fuels Fund alongside a statutory SAF mandate that requires sustainable fuels to account for a progressively larger proportion of aviation fuel demand.

Hydrogen Utopia's board believes these measures could create a supportive environment for waste-derived fuel projects. The company expects its new licence to improve its prospects of accessing public funding while providing a platform from which it can develop and scale waste-to-SAF infrastructure in the UK.

Despite the potential commercial opportunity, Hydrogen Utopia remains at an early stage financially. The company is pre-revenue, continues to report losses and has generated predominantly negative operating cash flow. Its technical picture is also weak, with the share price trading below important moving averages and the MACD indicator remaining negative.

Traditional valuation measures offer limited support at present because the company is loss-making, resulting in a negative price-to-earnings ratio, while it does not currently provide a dividend yield.

More about Hydrogen Utopia International PLC

Hydrogen Utopia International PLC develops waste-to-fuel technology designed to process non-recyclable mixed waste plastics into hydrogen, sustainable aviation fuel and other cleaner fuels, alongside advanced materials and renewable heat.

Its proposed facilities use waste that cannot otherwise be recycled as feedstock for the production of syngas. The company ultimately aims to generate revenue from the sale of gases, electricity and heat, as well as fees charged for processing waste, with its development strategy focused on markets offering supportive government policies and significant private-sector investment.

Hydrogen Utopia International PLC

(the "Company" or "HUI")

HUI secures UK Licence for SAF

Hydrogen Utopia International PLC HUI, a pioneering company transforming non-recyclable waste plastic into hydrogen, clean fuels and advanced materials, focusing on advanced fuels such as jet fuel and Sustainable Aviation Fuel ("SAF"), is pleased to announce that it has secured a licence from InEnTec Inc. ("InEnTec") to deploy its proven PEM® (Plasma Enhanced Melter) gasification technology for sustainable aviation fuel ("SAF") production, across the United Kingdom, for a total consideration of $500,000 ("UK Licence Agreement").

The UK Licence Agreement grants HUI rights to build, operate and scale PEM® Melter systems throughout the UK, converting non-recyclable mixed waste plastics, tyres and other hazardous and non-hazardous waste streams into clean syngas, a versatile building block for SAF production. InEnTec's PEM® gasification technology has been proven across more than a decade of commercial deployment worldwide, combining plasma arc technology with a molten glass bath to convert virtually any organic waste into ultra-clean syngas without combustion or incineration.

The UK Licence Agreement follows HUI's earlier exclusive licence with InEnTec covering the Middle East and North Africa ("MENA") region, secured for large-scale projects across Saudi Arabia and the wider GCC. The strong commercial interest and momentum seen in MENA has demonstrated clear demand for InEnTec's PEM® gasification technology at scale. The Board believes the UK market is now following that same trajectory underpinned by the Department of Transport's launch of the £219 million Low Carbon Fuels Fund ("LCFF") and the statutory SAF mandate. With licences now secured in both regions, HUI is building a growing international platform for PEM® gasification technology-based waste-to-fuel deployment.

The UK Licence Agreement is secured as the UK Government ramps up support for domestic low-carbon fuel production. The LCFF will make £93 million available over the next two years to UK-based companies to help scale SAF production, with support prioritised for projects closest to commercial deployment. The LCFF is projected to add £5 billion to the UK economy by 2050 and builds on the Government's existing £198 million Advanced Fuels Fund, which has been backing cleaner aviation technologies since 2022.

The LCFF has been introduced specifically to help the UK meet its statutory SAF mandate, which requires SAF to make up 10% of UK jet fuel demand by 2030, rising to 22% by 2040, a trajectory the Government estimates could deliver up to 6.3 million tonnes of annual carbon savings by 2040. The SAF mandate is technology-neutral across eligible production pathways. HUI's route to SAF is by conversion of non-recyclable waste plastic to syngas via InEnTec's PEM® gasification technology, which is then processed into SAF, giving the Company a distinct feedstock-driven pathway to help meet the SAF mandate. With SAF demand now mandated by law rather than being voluntary, the Board believes the UK market now offers a durable, policy-backed pathway for HUI to advance its mission of converting non-recyclable waste plastic into sustainable fuels, including through the waste-to-SAF infrastructure HUI is licensed to deploy.

The Board believes HUI's UK licence positions the Company strongly to seek LCFF support, given the potential for the licensed PEM® gasification technology to convert non-recyclable waste into syngas that can be further processed into low-carbon and sustainable fuels, in alignment with the fund's objectives.

The UK Licence Agreement has been secured for a total consideration of $500,000 of which $250,000 has been paid and the remaining $250,000 is payable by promissory note.

Aleksandra Binkowska, Chief Executive Officer of HUI, commented: "We are delighted to strengthen our partnership with Inentec, which operates the only commercially proven technology in its class. This positions us well for expansion into the UK, where the government is actively supporting the sustainable aviation fuel market. We expect to now accelerate our UK operation as we engage with feedstock suppliers, off take agreements and finalise discussions on location for the SAF facility."

text:
The US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has approved the use of oil from the winter oilseed crop CoverCress for renewable fuel production under the federal Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) program. The decision gives the crop access to the US biofuel market and lays the groundwork for expanding its commercial production.

Renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) produced from CoverCress oil under the approved pathways will qualify for D4 Renewable Identification Numbers (RINs). Renewable naphtha and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) produced from the same feedstock will qualify for D5 RINs. These credits are used by US fuel market participants to meet RFS obligations, making the approval an important factor in the commercial viability of the new feedstock.

CoverCress is a winter oilseed crop that can be integrated between major cash crops in a crop rotation. It is planted after the main crop is harvested in the fall and harvested before spring planting begins. This allows farmers to generate an additional crop and source of income from the same land while maintaining soil cover during the winter.

CoverCress is preparing for its first commercial crush in early 2027. EPA approval removes one of the key regulatory barriers to developing a new supply chain involving farmers, grain handlers, processors and renewable fuel producers.

The emergence of a new source of vegetable oil is particularly important amid growing US biofuel demand. The development of CoverCress could expand domestic supplies of oilseed feedstocks and provide an additional alternative to traditional biofuel feedstocks, including soybean and rapeseed oil.

Kapabar – Peringatan Hari Ulang Tahun (HUT) Kemerdekaan Republik Indonesia ke-81 menjadi momentum bersejarah bagi bangsa dalam mengukuhkan kemandirian dan kedaulatan energi nasional.

Dari ujung paling timur Nusantara, PT Pertamina Patra Niaga Refinery Unit Kasim mempersembahkan kado istimewa melalui keberhasilan lifting perdana produk Biosolar B50 yang telah dilakukan tahun ini sebagai langkah nyata menjalankan mandatory pemerintah sekaligus mewujudkan mimpi swasembada energi nasional.

Langkah strategis Kilang Kasim dalam merealisasikan Biosolar B50 ini bergerak selaras dengan arah kebijakan energi nasional dan Pesan Kemerdekaan Direktur Utama PT Pertamina (Persero) Simon Aloysius Mantiri.

Dalam amanatnya pada peringatan Kemerdekaan RI ke-81, Direktur Utama menegaskan komitmen perusahaan untuk terus mengakselerasi pengembangan portofolio energi hijau berkelanjutan.

“Pertamina terus melanjutkan program biodiesel menuju B50, mengembangkan rantai pasok bioetanol berbasis tebu, jagung, ketela, dan sorgum guna mendukung pencapaian target pencampuran E10 hingga E20 nasional, memanfaatkan minyak jelantah dan minyak nabati, serta mengembangkan Sustainable Aviation Fuel dan produk rendah karbon lainnya,” kata Simon dalam siaran persnya, Senin 17 Agustus 2026.

Menurut Simon, melalui strategi ini, Pertamina tidak hanya sedang membangun portofolio energi, melainkan sedang membangun sumber-sumber baru yang akan terus memberi energi bagi kemerdekaan Indonesia di masa depan.

Sebagai satu-satunya kilang pengolahan minyak di wilayah Indonesia Timur, Kilang Kasim terus membuktikan keunggulannya dalam mengadopsi teknologi dan standar operasional energi terbarukan.

Produk Biosolar B50 yang merupakan campuran 50 persen Fatty Acid Methyl Ester (FAME) berbasis minyak sawit dan 50 persen minyak solar menjadi bukti konkret kesiapan Kilang Kasim dalam mengoptimalkan potensi minyak nabati domestik, menurunkan jejak emisi karbon, serta mengikis ketergantungan pada impor bahan bakar fosil murni.

Kado dari Kilang Kasim ini sekaligus mempertegas bahwa keterbatasan geografis di kawasan timur bukan menjadi penghalang untuk melahirkan inovasi bahan bakar berkualitas tinggi bagi masyarakat Papua, Maluku, dan sekitarnya.

Momentum HUT RI ke-81 menjadi pengingat bahwa perjuangan mengisi kemerdekaan adalah estafet yang terus berjalan. Dari pulau kecil di kawasan Seget, Kilang Kasim membuktikan bahwa mimpi besar swasembada energi nasional dapat diwujudkan secara merata dari timur hingga barat Nusantara.

Dengan semangat kemerdekaan, PT Pertamina Patra Niaga RU Kasim berkomitmen untuk terus menjaga operasional kilang yang aman, handal, dan ramah lingkungan, demi memberi energi bagi masa depan Indonesia yang mandiri dan berdaulat. */RON

text:
A former Jetstar pilot has revealed how he became so concerned about climate change he decided to quit his job after 42 years in the industry and become a baker.

Geoff Collis, in his 60s, had always wanted to fly since the age of 10 and spent over four decades in the air despite hearing about 'the greenhouse effect' in the 1980s.

As information on the issue became more widespread, he began questioning whether his lifelong passion for planes was enough to outweigh the environmental impact of his job.

'I was just looking at the amount of fuel I was ordering for each flight … and I thought, "How can I justify continuing in this sort of role?"' he told the ABC.

'It was a 2.4million-litres-a-year jet fuel habit.'

Mr Collis got a taste of life outside of aviation when he was partially stood down during Covid, beginning a baking apprenticeship at Old Evropa Bakery in Eltham, Melbourne's north-east.

He resumed his piloting duties in 2023, but didn't last long because climate change weighed so much on his mind that he wasn't able to continue flying.

'I started to realise that most of what [the industry] appeared to be doing [for climate change] was really just tokenism, spin and greenwashing,' Mr Collis said.

'I got to the point where I just thought … I don't think I can, in clear conscience amidst the climate situation we're facing, be part of the industry anymore.

'Eventually, it was a no-brainer. I had really no option but to to to walk away from it.'

Mr Collis said a factor in his decision to resign was that the aviation industry reassured him that 'everything was under control' even though evidence suggested otherwise.

'I tried to find out what the airline industry was doing to reinvent itself for a carbon constrained future and realised that my first love wasn't being entirely truthful to me,' he told Flight Free Australia.

'Yes, the airline industry is slowly moving towards marginally more fuel efficient aircraft, but what they don't want you think about is that emissions from planned airline growth will totally swamp any small efficiency gains.

'Yes, the airline industry is beginning to implement supposedly lower impact technology such as so-called "sustainable aviation fuel" or SAF, but what they don't want to you consider is that there will never be anywhere near enough arable land or electricity generation capability for any of them at the scale required.

'Yes, the industry is working to improve efficiency in the air through direct tracking and better traffic management to reduce airborne holding time, but what they don't want you to know is that these are marginal tinkering gains at best.'

Mr Collis now works part-time as a baker at Old Evropa Bakery, but admitted he kept some doubts as to whether he made the right decision.

Those doubts eased when he discovered Safe Landing, a group established by current and former aviation workers to support pilots grappling with climate concerns.

'Knowing there are other people out there who came to the same conclusion as myself was reassuring and reaffirming,' he told the ABC.

'There was a huge sense of like, "Wow I'm not the only oddball who's feeling this way."'

While his love for flying will never die, Mr Collis said he has no regrets about moving on to the next chapter of his life.

description:

text:
Formula 1’s global logistics operation relies on a highly coordinated mix of airfreight, sea freight, road transport and venue infrastructure, with planning beginning months ahead to ensure equipment, teams and facilities reach each race on fixed timelines despite widely varying local conditions.

Calendar expansion is increasing pressure on the logistics network, making airport capacity, customs capability, road infrastructure and local support important considerations when assessing new venues. The challenge extends well beyond the circuit itself, encompassing freight, accommodation, staff, spectators and wider event infrastructure.

Sustainability is becoming integral to the logistics model, with Formula 1 and DHL Motorsport pursuing more efficient aircraft, HVO-powered European trucking, sustainable paddock power and route optimisation, while electrification is being adopted cautiously where technology can meet the reliability demands of a fixed, time-critical race calendar.

As Formula 1 continues to expand across continents, the logistics operation powering it has evolved to ensure it always delivers the race weekends on fixed timelines through a blend of airfreight, sea freight, road transport, venue planning and local infrastructure management.

The operational challenge is not simply moving equipment between events, but creating a repeatable framework that can adapt to different environments. From established European circuits to complex flyaway races, Formula 1’s logistics model relies on early planning, regional knowledge and the ability to respond when conditions change.

Building a global race operation

The foundations of each event are established months before cars reach the track. Formula 1’s operational teams begin venue preparation well ahead of race weekend, managing everything from paddock construction and technical requirements to the positioning of infrastructure. The scale of the task varies significantly depending on location, with venues such as Silverstone presenting challenges due to size, while street circuits create different logistical constraints due to narrow pitlanes and paddocks.

For DHL Motorsport, the focus is ensuring freight flows remain predictable despite changing borders, customs requirements and regional conditions. European races benefit from established movement patterns, while international events require closer coordination with local agents and partners to maintain operational continuity.

“Normally, the first crews arrive two weeks before the event starts. During that period, we control what is happening in the areas we operate, from track branding to the paddock build. Every single day is needed because the scale of the operation is enormous,” Christian Pollhammer, Operations Manager, Sporting at Formula 1, explained.

“In Europe, freight movement is relatively straightforward because we are within the Schengen area. The real complexity comes with international races, where we rely heavily on local agents and strong working relationships to manage customs and local requirements. That collaboration allows us to deliver consistently across very different environments,” Simon Price, Event Logistics Manager, DHL Motorsport, stated.

Capacity growth creates logistics pressure

The expansion of Formula 1 has increased the operational demands placed on the supply chain. More races, additional teams and growing commercial activity require greater volumes of equipment, more complex scheduling and stronger coordination between stakeholders. Logistics planning has therefore become an important consideration when assessing future venues and calendar development.

The decision to add or relocate events requires a detailed evaluation of infrastructure capability, including airports, freight handling capacity, road networks and local support. The ability to deliver a race depends on far more than the circuit itself, with the wider logistics ecosystem determining whether a venue can support the demands of a global championship.

“Everything is growing bigger, faster and that creates more challenges, but it is also a sign of success. More demand means we need larger structures to accommodate teams, sponsors and promoters. The challenge is balancing that growth with the logistics required to support it,” Pollhammer said.

“It is not just about staging a race and having 24 cars go around a circuit. You have freight arriving at airports, large volumes moving through customs, hundreds of containers arriving, thousands of staff requiring accommodation and hundreds of thousands of spectators coming to the event. There is a whole infrastructure required behind the race itself,” Price added.

Sustainability becomes a logistics priority

Alongside growth, sustainability has become a defining factor in Formula 1’s logistics strategy. Operational changes are focused on reducing emissions while maintaining the reliability required by a calendar where delays are not an option. Improvements include more efficient aircraft, sustainable aviation fuel, lower-emission road transport and regional equipment planning.

The transition reflects a wider challenge across global logistics: reducing environmental impact while preserving service performance. Electric transport is being explored, but infrastructure limitations mean adoption must be aligned with operational requirements. For Formula 1, sustainability measures must work within a highly time-sensitive environment.

“We have worked on optimising travel routes, although that is not always simple because race dates are fixed through long-term contracts. We have also introduced sustainable power supplies for paddocks and team areas using solar panels, batteries and lower-emission solutions. These steps are helping us reduce our footprint gradually,” Pollhammer outlined.

“We have moved from 747 aircraft towards 777 aircraft, which are more fuel efficient, and our European trucks use HVO fuel. We are also looking at electrification, but we need to make sure the technology can still deliver the service required. When it reaches the right level, we will move forward with it,” Price concluded.

text:
David Colindres, President of the San Marino Aircraft Registry (SMAR), manages the Republic of San Marino’s T7 civil aircraft registry, which serves a diverse international clientele including aircraft owners, operators, financiers, and lessors. While aircraft registries are commonly perceived as administrative entities responsible for registration marks, documentation, and compliance records, their function extends far beyond these tasks. They play a crucial role within the financial framework of the aviation industry.

Aircraft as Global Financial Assets

Aircraft represent some of the most valuable and globally mobile assets, frequently changing ownership, jurisdiction, and legal structures. For financial institutions, aircraft often serve as collateral in various financing arrangements, ranging from traditional loans to operating leases and more complex financial instruments. The registry’s capacity to function within a strong legal framework and maintain comprehensive documentation is vital. It ensures that ownership rights are clearly established, security interests are properly recorded, and the aircraft’s regulatory status remains transparent.

This legal clarity is fundamental for financiers assessing risk. Lenders require confidence that aircraft can be transferred or relocated efficiently in the event of ownership changes or the conclusion of financing agreements. Registries that operate under robust legal systems provide this certainty, thereby reducing the legal complexities and uncertainties inherent in cross-border transactions.

Challenges and Market Dynamics

The aviation financing landscape faces several challenges. Fluctuations in jet fuel prices and airline profitability can heighten the risk of default, potentially resulting in financial losses for lessors and financiers. To address these risks, market participants may need to renegotiate or restructure financing and leasing agreements to ensure airlines can fulfill their obligations. Competitors may respond by increasing borrowing costs or adopting alternative financing models, such as export credit-supported financing, to mitigate exposure.

Additionally, regulatory changes and variations in federal funding for airports introduce further complexity into the aviation financing environment. These evolving factors underscore the importance of a reliable and reputable aircraft registry, which becomes a critical element in the decision-making process for financiers and lessors.

Leasing and the Need for Flexibility

Leasing has emerged as a predominant model in the aviation sector, with many aircraft changing hands multiple times, particularly in commercial aviation and increasingly within business aviation. For lessors, operational flexibility is essential. A registry that provides a clear and predictable regulatory environment facilitates smoother transactions and supports the dynamic nature of aircraft ownership and leasing arrangements.

The Registry’s Pivotal Role

In the context of a global aviation industry where financing, registration, and operations frequently cross international borders, the integrity of the aircraft registry is fundamental to preserving asset value and enabling seamless transactions. A well-managed registry not only ensures compliance with regulatory requirements but also underpins the financial stability and adaptability demanded by modern aviation.

text:
The European planemaker enters the autumn stretch with two very different narratives competing for investor attention. One involves a rare technical incident in Indian airspace that has drawn regulators into a joint review; the other is a straightforward industrial arithmetic problem that will determine whether the company hits its full-year delivery target.

Neither, so far, has knocked the share price off its stride. The stock closed Friday at €215.75, a mere 2.5 percent below its 52-week high, with a 9.2 percent gain since January and an 18 percent advance over twelve months. The market's message is clear: it is looking past the noise.

A Triple Failure That Demands Answers

Aviation specialists were caught off guard by news that an Air India A320 experienced a triple hydraulic failure — an event so unusual that modern airliners are designed with redundant systems specifically to make it all but impossible. Airbus has opened a safety review alongside Indian authorities, a sign that both sides are treating the matter with the seriousness it warrants.

Details remain thin: no information has been released on injuries or the outcome of the affected flight. The incident adds to a string of recent events in Indian airspace that have sharpened scrutiny on carriers and suppliers operating in the region.

For investors, the question is whether this becomes a systemic concern for the A320 fleet or fades as an isolated case. So far, the market has chosen the latter interpretation. The shares have climbed roughly 40 percent from their March low, suggesting that safety headlines of this kind are being priced as one-off events rather than structural risks.

Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying Airbus?

The Delivery Gap Widens

The more pressing issue for the stock may be the factory floor. July saw 67 aircraft handed over to 39 customers — a figure that leaves the company with a significant gap to close if it is to meet its 870-unit target for the year. With 418 deliveries banked by the end of July, the remaining five months require an average of roughly 90 aircraft per month, a pace the company has not consistently sustained.

The July mix tells its own story about where demand is heading. The A321neo accounted for 37 of the month's deliveries, with 18 A320neo, six A220-300s, and six A350-family aircraft rounding out the tally. The continued tilt toward the larger narrowbody reflects airlines' preference for higher-capacity single-aisle jets.

Orders Tell a Brighter Tale

If deliveries are lagging, the order book is thriving. Airbus crossed the 1,000 net-order threshold for the year in July, helped by more than 200 new bookings during the month alone. Confirmed deals include China Eastern Airlines' order for 25 A330-900s and an agreement with Hainan Airlines covering 40 A320neo-family aircraft.

Another large contract appears to be taking shape: Biman Bangladesh Airlines is expected to sign a multi-billion-dollar deal for ten aircraft by the end of August, with deliveries scheduled to begin in 2031. The pipeline suggests that demand for the company's products remains robust even as production struggles to keep pace.

Anchors Beyond the Delivery Schedule

Management has been careful to give investors reasons to look beyond the short-term delivery gap. The board has approved a €5 billion share buyback program spread over three years, contingent on ongoing shareholder approval. The company has also reaffirmed its target of €12 to €13 billion in adjusted operating profit for 2029, based on an exchange rate of $1.22 per euro.

The valuation picture is more mixed. Simply Wall St calculates a fair value of €219.32 per share, implying the stock is modestly undervalued on fundamentals. Sadif Investment Analytics, however, downgraded the shares from "Buy" to "Hold" on August 11, trimming its price target from €228.14 to €201.51 — a sign that the recent rally may have consumed much of the near-term upside.

Diversification as a Buffer

Meanwhile, the company continues to advance on multiple fronts beyond commercial aviation. The European Space Agency and Eumetsat have awarded Airbus the contract for the Aeolus-2 satellite, which will carry a Doppler wind lidar to improve weather forecasting. The predecessor satellite, launched in 2018, improved forecast accuracy by four percent, according to the company.

Airbus at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now.

On the sustainability front, Chief Sustainability Officer Julie Kitcher told the Farnborough air show that the focus is shifting toward pragmatic implementation — including the expansion of sustainable aviation fuel partnerships with Air Canada and next-generation aircraft that Kitcher says will burn 20 to 25 percent less fuel.

A test flight of the A350-1000ULR also turned heads: the long-range aircraft covered roughly 17,000 kilometers between Toulouse and Melbourne in under 19 hours, part of preparations for Qantas' Project Sunrise and its planned nonstop routes such as Sydney-London.

A three-year flight test campaign using an A321neo demonstrator will explore folding wingtips with high aspect ratios under the "Wing of Tomorrow" program — technology aimed at future efficiency gains rather than near-term earnings.

That breadth — spanning civil aviation, space, and sustainability initiatives — helps explain why investors have so far shrugged off both the safety review and the delivery shortfall. The question now is whether the factory can deliver on its promises before the market's patience runs out.

title: Beyond Petrol and EVs: Toyota's flex-fuel Hycross shows what E85 could mean for India
description:
Here are all the key changes that help the Hycross TNGA 2.0-litre strong hybrid become compatible with E85 fuel.
Three-Way Catalytic Converter These flex-fuel vehicles use a three-way catalytic converter to significantly reduce emissions.
Changes to the Fuel Tank The fuel tank and fuel pipes of the E85 vehicle have been treated with a special coating to make them more resistant to corrosion.
The flex-fuel Hycross was showcased alongside a couple of other vehicles modified by OEMs to adapt to different grades of ethanol-blended fuel.
He explained that flex-fuel vehicles would not be restricted to running on E85 alone.
text:
India’s push towards cleaner fuels is closely tied to how quickly automakers can adapt their vehicles to run efficiently on higher ethanol blends. As the country moves towards greater ethanol adoption to reduce its dependence on conventional fuels and cut emissions, vehicle technology will play a crucial role in making the transition practical. Toyota has been among the automakers working to ensure its vehicles can adapt to higher ethanol-blended fuels without compromising everyday usability.

Recently, we had the chance to get up close with the Toyota Innova Hycross electrified flex-fuel prototype at the India Big Energy and Tech Expo. It was during our intensive walkaround of the vehicle that we identified the changes that help the normal, run-of-the-mill Innova Hycross hybrid run on higher ethanol blends.

Here are all the key changes that help the Hycross TNGA 2.0-litre strong hybrid become compatible with E85 fuel.

Improved Corrosion Resistance Within the Engine

Since ethanol is more acidic and has a higher capacity to absorb water, engines that run on high-ethanol blends face a greater risk of corrosion. To ensure that the engine ancillaries can function reliably with such fuel, the prototype gets ethanol-compatible spark plugs, valves, valve seats and piston rings, which are designed to resist corrosion and improve wear resistance.

Essentially, components that come directly in contact with high-ethanol fuel have received similar treatment to ensure they can withstand its properties.

Three-Way Catalytic Converter

These flex-fuel vehicles use a three-way catalytic converter to significantly reduce emissions. The converter has been modified because the combustion of ethanol produces a different mix of hydrocarbons, along with NOx and carbon emissions, compared with regular petrol. This helps the vehicle comply with BS6 Phase 2 emission norms.

Advanced High-Pressure Fuel Injectors

With ethanol-heavy fuel blends, the fuel mixture tends to burn at a higher temperature than gasoline, and the engine often requires high-pressure injectors to generate the necessary performance.

The ethanol-powered Hycross employs high-pressure injectors that not only provide the required flow rate but have also been specifically designed to handle higher temperatures and resist corrosion.

Changes to the Fuel Tank

The fuel tank and fuel pipes of the E85 vehicle have been treated with a special coating to make them more resistant to corrosion.

While the ethanol content in the E20 blend mandated for users is much lower, reports from ARAI and SIAM have highlighted the possibility of rubber components in the fuel supply system of legacy vehicles wearing out earlier than expected.

Changes to the ECU

With these fuel-system changes, the ECU also had to be tuned based on factors such as compression, back pressure and how lean or rich the fuel mixture is throughout the combustion cycle.

The ECU has been calibrated to adapt to different blends, ranging from E20 to E85 and even pure petrol.

Specialized Ethanol Sensor

A key addition to the regular Hycross in the flex-fuel MPV segment is the presence of an ethanol sensor. The sensor measures the concentration of ethanol in the fuel and relays this information to the specialized ECU, which can then electronically adjust various aspects of engine operation.

The sensor can recognize the ethanol blend and manage engine operations according to the fuel available. The flex-fuel variant of the Innova Hycross is also capable of running on electric power for up to 60% of the time and on biofuel for the rest, potentially making it more economical and environmentally friendly.

Motor-Driven VVT Module

Conventional gasoline engines can generally start at temperatures below zero, but ethanol's higher ignition temperature can create cold-start issues and make the engine take longer to start.

With the changes made to the Hycross, the car is expected to be able to start at temperatures as low as -15 degrees Celsius. An independent VVT module would further help the manufacturer manage valve-lift timings according to engine conditions, enhancing efficiency.

Generally, these timings are manipulated through different cam profiles and actuators that are triggered to change the cam profiles on the go.

The Innova Hycross was not the only vehicle to feature such changes to its drivetrain. A similarly equipped Camry was also placed alongside it. The flex-fuel Hycross was showcased alongside a couple of other vehicles modified by OEMs to adapt to different grades of ethanol-blended fuel.

Hero and TVS also showcased a plethora of new and upcoming variants that are still in the early stages of development but could soon offer riders a wider choice of environmentally friendly vehicles.

The India Big Energy and Tech Expo, jointly organized by IFGE and MM Activ Sci-Tech Communications, highlighted the various bioenergy avenues that the government is exploring as part of its efforts towards a more carbon-neutral future.

Adding further clarity to the potential of flex-fuel vehicles, Vaibhav Dange, Founder-Director of the Indian Federation of Green Energy, sought to clear up a common misconception around E85 fuel. He explained that flex-fuel vehicles would not be restricted to running on E85 alone. Instead, they would give consumers greater freedom to choose their fuel, allowing the vehicle to run on any blend ranging from 100% petrol to 100% ethanol, depending on availability and price.

“The consumer should have the choice,” he said, arguing that flex-fuel technology could give motorists greater control over the type of fuel they use.

He pointed to Brazil as an example, where flex-fuel vehicles are already widely used. According to him, the technology gives consumers greater fuel choice and sovereignty, particularly when ethanol becomes more affordable. “I can drive a car on any blend from 100% petrol to 100% ethanol,” he explained.

Beyond the momentum towards greener fuels and increased consumer choice, Dange also highlighted the broader potential of bioenergy. He described bioenergy as a spectrum, covering everything from agricultural and municipal waste to different forms of biomass.

“Bioenergy is a spectrum: sugarcane, maize, broken rice, any grain that is not suitable for human consumption; ethanol is produced from it. Now, second-generation ethanol is produced from bamboo, rice straw or bagasse. So, it is also being used.

“From the amount of bio-waste, agri-waste or municipal solid waste, CBG is produced. After purifying it, it becomes CNG, which can be used in vehicles or as piped natural gas.

“From this, sustainable aviation fuel can be produced. Sustainable aviation fuel can be used for aviation. Biomass can be used to produce biochar, pellets and briquettes.

“Seven per cent of our thermal plants are advised to use biomass for carbon reduction. We can make biochar from biomass. Furthermore, the plastic, glass or plastic bottles that we use can be made from biomass or biomaterials. It will be biodegradable. So, there are so many opportunities for bioenergy that are opening up.”

As the Indian automotive industry grapples with the eventual shift from gasoline-powered vehicles towards hybrids and EVs, flex-fuel vehicles could offer consumers another option in the transition. The technology could give motorists greater flexibility in choosing their fuel while allowing automakers to make use of India's growing ethanol ecosystem.

However, how this new class of vehicles fares in the Indian market remains to be seen. Beyond automobiles, the wider range of bioenergy solutions being explored — from CBG and sustainable aviation fuel to biochar and biomaterials — could also play an important role in India's efforts to build a cleaner and more diverse energy ecosystem.

제품정보

수송 바이오 연료 시장은 수송을 위한 재생 가능 생물학 물자에게서 한 연료의 생산, 가공, 배급 및 사용을 포함합니다. 주요 연료에는 에탄올, 바이오 디젤, 재생 가능한 디젤 및 지속 가능한 항공 연료가 포함됩니다. 시장 기회는 폐기물 기반 연료, 고급 바이오 연료 기술을 통해 성장하고 있으며, 같은 재료의 사용 식용유 농업 잔류물.

2026 년 4 월, 인도 정부는 항공 연료와 혼합 된 지속 가능한 항공 연료를 포함하는 항공 터빈 연료 제어 명령을 개정했습니다. 인도는 또한 SAF 블렌딩 대상을 2027 년에 1 %, 2028 년 2 %, 국제 비행을위한 2030 %를 나타냅니다. 이 이니셔티브는 SAF에 대한 수요를 창출하고 항공의 생산, 공급 및 사용을 격려함으로써 운송 바이오 연료 시장을 지원합니다.

1. Renewable 연료 생산 확장

기업은 더 청결한 수송 연료를 위한 수요를 충족시키기 위하여 재생 가능 연료의 생산을 증가합니다. 새로운 식물에 투자하고 기존의 시설을 확장하고 생산 공정을 개선합니다. 더 높은 생산은 회사는 도로 수송, 항공 및 다른 수송 분야에 더 연료를 공급하는 것을 돕습니다.

2. 지속 가능한 항공 연료 수용량

3. 폐기물 기반 Feedstocks 사용

회사는 사용 된 요리 오일, 동물 지방 및 농업 폐기물과 같은 폐기물 재료를 사용하여 운송 바이오 연료를 생산합니다. 이러한 자료를 사용하여 회사는 전통적인 원료에 따라 다른 연료의 다른 소스를 개발하는 데 도움이됩니다. 또한 바이오 연료 생산을 확장하는 노력도 지원합니다.

4. 팽창 에탄올 생산

회사는 차량에 대한 더 많은 연료를 공급하는 에탄올 생산을 확장하고 있습니다. 그들은 식물 수용량을 증가하고 옥수수와 설탕과 같은 농업 물자를 사용하여 에타놀을 만들기 위하여 증가합니다. Higher 생산은 회사가 가솔린과 혼합하여 더 많은 에탄올을 공급하고 운송 연료 시장에서 더 강력하게 경쟁 할 수 있습니다.

1. 둥지

본부: Espoo, 핀란드

Neste는 재생 가능한 디젤 및 지속 가능한 항공 연료 (SAF)를 생산함으로써 글로벌 운송 바이오 연료 시장에서 주로 경쟁합니다. 이 회사는 재생 가능한 원료에서 재생 가능 연료를 만듭니다. 재생 가능한 제품 생산 능력은 2027 년에 연간 6.8 백만 톤에 도달 할 계획입니다. 4월 2025일, Neste는 네덜란드 로테르담의 정유 공장에서 SAF를 생산하기 시작했습니다. 정유 공장은 년 당 SAF의 500,000 톤까지 생성할 수 있고, Neste의 총 SAF 생산 능력은 년 당 1.5 백만 톤에 달합니다. 또한 항공사와 다른 고객과 협력하여 재생 가능한 연료의 사용을 늘리고 있습니다.

2. Valero 에너지 기업

본부: 샌안토니오, 텍사스, 미국

Valero는 에탄올 및 재생 가능한 디젤을 생산하여 운송 바이오 연료 시장에 참여합니다. 회사는 미국에 있는 12의 에탄올 식물을, 년 당 1.7 억 갤런의 총 생산 능력과 더불어 운영합니다. Valero는 다이아몬드 그린 디젤 (DGD)의 파트너이며 루이지애나와 텍사스에서 재생 가능한 연료 식물을 운영합니다. DGD는 연간 최대 1.2 억 갤런의 재생 가능한 디젤 생산 능력을 가지고 있으며 SAF의 235 백만 갤런까지. Valero는 미국, 캐나다 및 영국에 14개의 정유소를 운영합니다. 신재생 디젤 사업은 기존 연료와 함께 낮은 탄소 운송 연료를 생산할 수 있습니다.

2. 명세

Headquarters: 시카고, 일리노이, 미국

ADM은 바이오 에탄올 및 바이오 디젤 생산을 통해 주로 운송 바이오 연료 시장에서 경쟁합니다. 이 회사는 옥수수와 식물성 기름과 같은 농업 재료를 사용하여 운송 연료를 만듭니다. ADM는 에탄올이 휘발유와 혼합 될 수 있다고 주장하며, 바이오 디젤은 기존의 디젤에 대안으로 사용될 수 있습니다. 이 회사는 대형 농업 처리 네트워크, 270 개 이상의 가공 공장, 470 개 이상의 농산물 조달 시설 및 운영 140 개 이상의 국가. 2025년 동안 ADM의 에탄올 사업은 미국 바이오 연료 정책의 변화에 영향을 미쳤습니다.

4. POET

본부: Sioux Falls, 사우스 다코타, 미국

POET는 bioethanol 생산을 통해서 수송 바이오 연료 시장에 주로 집중됩니다. 회사는 옥수수에서 bioethanol를 만들고 국내와 국제 시장에 공급합니다. POET는 35 생물 처리 시설을 운영하고 있으며 약 3.1 억 갤런의 연간 바이오 에탄올 생산 능력이 있습니다. 회사는 30,000 개 이상의 농부와 함께 작동합니다. 2025년에, POET는 Tennessee에 있는 녹색 평야 Obion를, 연례 bioethanol 수용량의 120백만개 갤런 추가했습니다. 2 월 2025에서 POET는 Nebraska 시설에 연결 된 탄소 캡처 프로젝트에 Tallgrass과 함께 일했습니다.

5. Chevron 기업

Headquarters: 휴스턴, 텍사스, 미국

Chevron은 재생 가능한 디젤, 바이오 디젤 및 지속 가능한 항공 연료를 통해 운송 바이오 연료 시장에 참여합니다. 이 회사는 식물성 기름, 동물성 지방 및 사용 된 요리 기름과 같은 재료를 사용하여 재생 가능 연료를 만듭니다. 2025 년 Chevron은 Geismar의 확장을 완료, 루이지애나 재생 가능한 디젤 공장, 연간 340 백만 갤런에 생산 능력을 증가. Chevron은 Louisiana의 석유 가공 공장의 건설을 통해 Bunge와 합작 투자를 계속했습니다. 식물은 바이오 연료를 만들기 위해 사용되는 원료의 공급을 지원합니다.

6. 레이젠

Headquarters: São Paulo, 브라질

Raízen은 Sugarcane 기반 에탄올 및 두 번째 세대 에탄올 (E2G)을 통해 운송 바이오 연료 시장에서 경쟁합니다. 회사는 설탕과 짚에서 일정한 에타놀 그리고 E2G를 만듭니다. Raízen은 24 설탕, 에탄올 및 바이오에너지 선반과 70 이상의 연료 배급 맨끝. E2G는 일반적인 작물만을 사용하는 대신 설탕에서 왼쪽으로 농업 재료를 사용합니다. Raízen은 동일한 설탕 생산에서 더 많은 바이오 연료를 만들 수 있습니다. 또한 파트너와 협력하여 E2G 기술을 개발하고 확장합니다.

7. 총 에너지

본부: Courbevoie, 프랑스

TotalEnergies는 바이오 디젤 및 지속 가능한 항공 연료를 통해 운송 바이오 연료 시장에서 경쟁합니다. 회사는 프랑스에서 biorefineries로 몇몇 전통적인 정유를 바꿨습니다. 이 시설은 사용 된 요리 오일 및 동물 지방과 같은 폐기물 재료를 사용하여 바이오 연료를 만듭니다. Grandpuits biorefinery는 SAF 생산 능력으로 개발되고, 노르망디와 La Mède 사이트도 생산 또는 프로세스 SAF. 2025년, TotalEnergies는 Quatra와 15년 계약에 서명하여 연간 60,000톤의 사용식유를 받을 수 있었습니다. 물자는 도로 바이오 연료와 SAF의 생산을 지원할 것입니다.

8. 에니

Headquarters: 로마, 이탈리아

Eni는 Enilive 비즈니스를 통해 HVO 재생 디젤, SAF 및 기타 바이오 연료를 통해 교통 바이오 연료 시장에서 경쟁합니다. Enilive는 이탈리아의 생분해를 운영하고 있으며 미국과 아시아에 활동을 확장했습니다. 2025년에, Enilive는 생물 정제 수용량의 년 당 1.65 백만 톤이 있고 바이오 연료의 925,000 톤을 판매했습니다. 2025 년 중요한 개발은 Gela, Italy, South Korea의 HVO 및 SAF 공장 건설 및 말레이시아의 Pengerang Biorefinery 개발의 시작을 포함했습니다.

9. VERBIO

본사: Zörbig, 독일

VERBIO는 바이오 디젤, 바이오 에탄올 및 바이오 메탄을 통해 운송 바이오 연료 시장에서 경쟁합니다. 이 회사는 바이오 매스 및 농업 폐기물을 재생 연료로 변환합니다. VERBIO는 유럽, 북미 및 아시아에서 생산 시설을 보유하고 있습니다. 2024/25년 동안, 회사는 biomethane의 1,190 GWh와 함께 바이오 디젤과 바이오 에탄올의 1.2 백만 톤 이상을 생산했습니다. 네바다, 아이오와 시설은 북미에서 회사의 확장의 중요한 부분이었습니다. VERBIO의 다른 재생 가능한 연료의 생산은 여러 운송 연료 시장을 제공 할 수 있습니다.

10. 윌마르 국제

본사: 싱가포르

Wilmar International은 팜 기반 바이오 디젤을 통해 운송 바이오 연료 시장에 주로 참여합니다. 회사는 말레이시아와 인도네시아의 시설에서 팜 기반 재료에서 바이오 디젤을 생산합니다. Wilmar는 통합 공급망 처리 플랜트, 처리 및 배포를 갖추고 있습니다. 이것은 그것의 biodiesel 생산 활동을 포함합니다. 이 작업은 운송용으로 바이오 디젤의 처리 및 유통을 갖춘 팜 기반 원료의 공급을 연결합니다.
